trade_offs.description: Each source table in scope becomes its own collection, with one exception: reviewable_notes is embedded in reviewables as a notes array.
trade_offs.impact: Collections keep the relational shape the application already reads, so the move changes the query syntax and the id handling, not the data model. Joins that the source ran inside the database are now one lookup or an application-side merge.

trade_offs.description: The notes array in reviewables is bounded by the application at 50 entries. The average is 3.33 notes per reviewable (an assumed count), so the document averages 2.2 KB and stays under 18.2 KB at the cap.
trade_offs.impact: The 16 MB document limit is never close. The application must reject a 51st note or move older notes out, because DocumentDB does not enforce the cap.

trade_offs.description: Row counts for most tables are assumed (the source reported no count), so document sizes and index sizes rest on the measured table size divided by the declared row width.
trade_offs.impact: Sizing figures are placeholders until a real count is taken before cutover. The api_keys figure of 71.68 KB comes from a one-row table size that includes index overhead, so the real document is far smaller.

trade_offs.description: Only indexes that serve an observed query are created. The source secondary indexes that no observed query reads, and the source unique constraints on those columns, are not carried over.
trade_offs.impact: Writes are cheaper and the working set is smaller. Uniqueness that the application relied on the database to enforce, such as unique names on ai_mcp_servers and ai_secrets, is not enforced until a unique index is added. Add them before cutover where the application depends on them.

trade_offs.description: Source ids come from sequences. Existing ids are kept as _id values, and new documents need ids generated by the application, as the color scheme insert does.
trade_offs.impact: The application owns id allocation after the move, so it needs a counter or another id generator that does not collide with the migrated ids.

trade_offs.description: Two reads filter with a not-equal test on status, and the token log retention delete uses a not-in list on action. DocumentDB cannot use an index for negation, so these filters run after the index scan on the other fields.
trade_offs.impact: The index still narrows by locale or by created_at, so these tables, which hold tens of rows, stay fast. A large table would need the negated field added as a positive filter.

trade_offs.description: The stale API client report uses a correlated lookup (let and pipeline) to find clients with no recently used key, which needs DocumentDB 8.0.2 or later on an instance-based cluster. The child theme join uses a plain equality lookup, which runs on every version.
trade_offs.impact: The target cluster must run 8.0.2 or later for the client report. The alternative is two reads merged in the application.

trade_offs.description: The form template lookup returns only the template id, so it reads the join collection and skips the template collection. The source join also confirmed the template exists.
trade_offs.impact: The application treats a missing template as possible only if a template is deleted without removing its category links; deleting a template must also delete its links.

trade_offs.description: Set-based writes (the base scheme repoint, the region renames, and the retention deletes) run as updateMany and deleteMany over an index and are not collection scans.
trade_offs.impact: Each write runs as a single command without a multi-document transaction, so a failure part way leaves some documents updated. The jobs are safe to re-run, and large deletes should run in batches.

trade_offs.description: The retention delete of rejected incoming emails uses a partial index on created_at limited to documents that have a rejection message, so rows with no message must omit the field instead of storing null.
trade_offs.impact: The migration must drop null rejection_message values when loading, and the application must not write null for that field.

trade_offs.description: Inet and uuid columns become strings, timestamps become dates, and jsonb or json columns become embedded documents. Credentials such as secrets, tokens and password hashes keep their values and should be encrypted at rest and restricted by role.
trade_offs.impact: Address and uuid comparisons become string comparisons, so range queries on addresses are no longer possible in the database. The credential collections need their own access policy.

trade_offs.description: Source triggers and the badge_posts view guard or read tables that stay on other engines. No application logic in this design replaces them.
trade_offs.impact: Read-only guards on the trigger-protected tables stay with those tables, and anything that read the view needs its own query path.
